text: Wrapping a lookup in an error handler seems like an obvious good habit — until you realize IFERROR can't tell an expected miss apart from an actually broken formula.

IFERROR replaces any error at all — #N/A, #REF!, #VALUE!, #NAME? — with one fallback value. That's exactly the problem: a deleted column producing #REF! gets the same friendly "Not found" message as a genuinely missing lookup value, so a real bug can hide behind that message indefinitely.

IFNA catches only #N/A, the "no match found" error, and lets every other error type display normally. That's the more honest default for a lookup — a missing match is expected and gets a clean fallback, but a broken reference stays loud and visible until someone actually fixes it.
That's the end of Chapter 2. Chapter 3 moves into aggregation and logic functions, starting with SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, and AVERAGEIFS.
